reason: Under an Important note the quote states the EventBridge rule, Lambda function, SNS topic and SQS queue used with lifecycle hooks must always be in the same Region as the Auto Scaling group.

The quotes support no notification target for a user data script, the CompleteLifecycleAction call and the IAM role, but they say the call is needed to signal that the action is complete, not that it is the only way to end the wait (the claim's 'to end the wait it must call' says more than the quote).
The quote says it is important to create a corresponding scale-in event for each scale-out event so resources match demand as closely as possible.
Under 'Scale out' the quotes state launched instances start in Pending and enter InService when fully configured and passing the Amazon EC2 health checks.
The quote describes Custom policy as a custom minimum and maximum range of capacity available when replacing instances, to balance cost and availability.
The quote states an instance maintenance policy only applies to instance maintenance events and doesn't prevent manual or automatic scaling.
The quote states a new instance must be provisioned before an existing one can be terminated and that this favors availability over cost savings.
Under the minimum healthy percentage concept the quote states a low value replaces instances faster but can reduce availability without enough healthy instances.
The quote states the default for a group is to not have an instance maintenance policy, so it responds to maintenance events with the default behaviors.
The quote states new instances are provisioned at the same time existing ones are terminated and that this favors cost savings over availability.

The quotes and their list context name unexpected termination, EC2 scheduled events and Spot interruptions as cases that default to terminate and launch, so capacity can fall below the lower threshold.
The quotes state manual scaling is the most basic way to scale and that you either update the desired capacity or terminate instances in the group.
The quote states replacements usually happen one at a time, but a lifetime too short to replace individually leads to several at once, by up to 10 percent of current capacity.
The quotes state a value of 0 clears a previously set value and that the setting applies to all current and future instances in the group.
Under 'Limitations' the quote states Auto Scaling will not terminate a scale-in protected instance even if it has reached its maximum instance lifetime.
The quote states you must specify a value of at least 86,400 seconds (one day) and that 0 clears a previous value, matching the condition qualifier.
The quote states you cannot set the maximum instance lifetime when creating a group in the console; the context adds you can edit the group afterwards.
The quote defines the maximum time in seconds an instance can be in service before it is terminated and replaced, with replacement on a schedule for security or compliance as a common use case.
The quote states the replacement uses the launch template or configuration currently associated with the group, so a different application version in its AMI is deployed automatically.
The quote states by default the instance is terminated and a new one launched while it terminates, and an instance maintenance policy can change this to launch before terminating.
The quote states expressions must eventually return a single time series; the same considerations list allows any available CloudWatch metric and any supported function.
The quote states Auto Scaling ensures the group never goes below the specified minimum and never goes above the specified maximum number of instances.
The quote states each active policy determines desired capacity independently and the maximum is used, with the same 10 versus 8 example giving 10.
The quote states that without Capacity Rebalancing, Spot Instances are not replaced until after the Spot service interrupts them and their health check fails.
The quotes recommend never putting confidential or sensitive information in user data, tags or free-form text fields such as a Name field.
The quote states by default Auto Scaling has no visibility into applications and can terminate instances before they gracefully shut down or complete their jobs.
Under the supported Capacity Reservation types the quote states On-Demand Capacity Reservations reserve compute capacity in a specific Availability Zone with no term commitment.
Under the prioritized strategy the quotes state launch order follows the override list and the Reserved Instance rate applies to matching types; the context gives the unused c4.large example.
The quote states Auto Scaling detects unreliable CloudWatch metrics behind scaling policies and pauses scale-in when reliable metrics are not available, such as missing data points.
The quote states predictive scaling analyzes metric data from up to the past 14 days to identify patterns.
The quote states the core assumption of a homogenous group with equal-capacity instances and that forecasts can otherwise be inaccurate; the context names mixed instances groups.
The quotes state that on a forecast decrease it will not scale in to remove capacity and that dynamic scaling policies must be created to remove capacity.
The quote states predictive scaling generates an hourly forecast of capacity requirements for the next 48 hours.
The quotes state predictive scaling first runs in forecast only mode, which generates forecasts but does not scale the group.
The quote states the forecast is updated every 6 hours using the latest CloudWatch data.
The quote recommends predictive scaling for regular traffic patterns and long-initializing applications because it launches capacity before forecasted load, unlike reactive dynamic scaling.
The quote states the maximum capacity can be automatically increased when the forecast approaches or exceeds it, using MaxCapacityBreachBehavior and MaxCapacityBuffer.
The quote states the metric must have at least 24 hours of data for predictive scaling to start forecasting.
The quote states a new group that replaces a deleted old one needs 24 hours of historical load data before forecasts start again.
The quote states SchedulingBufferTime (Pre-launch instances in the console) sets an earlier start so instances launch ahead of forecasted demand; the context gives the start-of-hour default.
